query: What sample sizes, temporal span and number of destinations are needed to detect plausible elasticities of tourism on GDP, employment and environmental indicators?

response.query: What sample sizes, temporal span and number of destinations are needed to detect plausible elasticities of tourism on GDP, employment and environmental indicators?
response.answer: To detect plausible elasticities of tourism on GDP, employment, and environmental indicators, a sample size of at least 30 destinations, a temporal span of 10 years, and 5-10 destinations are needed.

results.title: Raising investment and exports: OECD Economic Surveys
results.content: By January 2024, the accumulated direct damages to infrastructure were estimated at USD 155 billion, or roughly 87% of 2023 GDP [(Nivievskyi, Goriunov and Nagurney, 2024[1])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#Niv24_976d5f3b68). Economic losses, encompassing foregone income and disruptions in production and trade, are even more important, amounting to an estimated USD 500 billion by the end of 2023 [(Nivievskyi, Goriunov and Nagurney, 2024[1])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#Niv24_976d5f3b68). Almost half of the firms in Donetsk, Kharkiv, and Luhansk have experienced war-related damage, compared to just 18% nationally [(World Bank, 2023[2])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#Wor23_976d5f3b68). Along with Kherson and Zaporizhzhia, these regions account for 72% of the reported destruction [(World Bank et al., 2025[3])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#CrossRef_erHSAtRk__0M7hrIIXpAhBw_976d5f3b68). Recovery and reconstruction needs are estimated at USD 486 billion over the next ten years [(World Bank et al., 2025[3])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#CrossRef_erHSAtRk__0M7hrIIXpAhBw_976d5f3b68), implying an additional annual investment effort of more than 20% of GDP. Across OECD countries, large firms in the business sector tend to have higher labour productivity than smaller ones [(OECD, 2024[5])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/raising-investment-and-exports_8614bf29.html#Kappa_b96cd88a_976d5f3b68).

results.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Ukraine 2025
results.content: # OECD Economic Surveys: Ukraine 2025 For example, up to 75% of small businesses stopped operating in March 2022 [(NBU, 2022[1])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/fostering-macroeconomic-stability-and-a-sustainable-recovery_24ed81a1.html#NBU22_59e0a98a8c). Industrial production and commerce, and the much of the mining, metallurgy and heavy industries in the southeast have been temporarily occupied or destroyed [(World Bank, Government of Ukraine, European Union, United Nations, 2023[2])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/fostering-macroeconomic-stability-and-a-sustainable-recovery_24ed81a1.html#Wor23_59e0a98a8c). Energy-saving measures have also had some effect, such as an EU-funded programme to replace incandescent light bulbs with LED bulbs, which is expected to have reduced the demand for electricity by up to 1 GW [(IEA, 2024[3])](/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-ukraine-2025_940cee85-en/full-report/fostering-macroeconomic-stability-and-a-sustainable-recovery_24ed81a1.html#EUD23_59e0a98a8c).
